newsitem.title: CHINA: Ford says to launch China truck in December.
newsitem.headline: Ford says to launch China truck in December.

text.p: Ford Motor Co. will start production of a line of commercial trucks in China this December, a senior company official said Wednesday.

Ford and China's Jiangling Motors Corp., in which Ford has a 20 percent stake, would make about 20,000 of the Transit model vehicles in the first year of production, said Ford China President Vaughn Koshkarian.
"We are really enthusiastic about it in terms of starting production in December," Koshkarian said, adding he hoped output would rise to an annual 60,000 units within several years.

The Transit, which will be available first in a passenger bus version and later as a van and a truck, would be made from about 50 percent local parts, including a diesel engine built by Jiangling, Koshkarian said.
Ford will increase the localisation rate to 80 percent to 90 percent within two or three years, he said.
Ford was also considering boosting its stake in Jiangling to 30 percent by buying $54.5 million of foreign currency B shares the Chinese firm is to issue this month, he said.
Jiangling is already listed on China's southern Shenzhen stock exchange and said its net profit for 1996 soared 776 percent to 34.6 million yuan ($4.1 million).

Ford, which lost out to General Motors Corp. in bidding to set up a huge joint venture car plant in Shanghai, was also in talks to start making passenger cars, Koshkarian said, declining to give further details.
